title_yt: A Stranger Offers You This Coin Flip... Do You? #Shorts
title_fb: May stranger na nag-alok ng coin flip... G ka ba?
hook: What if a stranger offers: heads, win $150. Tails, lose $100?
open_loop: Line 3 ('Weird part? He's the one who should run.') plants a question about the stranger: why should the guy offering the deal be scared? Lines 4-7 are Benny's own story (he runs, comes back, loses flip #1, keeps flipping and wins the long game). The stranger half is paid off only in line 8, about 5 s from the end: every flip costs HIM $25.
payoff: Your brain makes the $100 loss feel like about $195 (loss aversion, about 2x), so you want to run. But each flip pays you +$25 on average, and after 100 flips you almost never end up behind (1.76%). Twist: the scary stranger is the one losing, $25 a flip, and he gulps.

facts_used.claim: In the coin toss (win $150 / lose $100), most people decline (the 'Nope! You run.' reaction).
Most people reject the 50/50 win $150 / lose $100 flip even though it is positive on average (corroborating).
Losses are treated as about twice as large as an equivalent gain; named loss aversion (on-screen 'LOSS AVERSION ~2x').
Meta-analysis mean loss-aversion coefficient 1.955, so a $100 loss feels like about $195.
+$25 average per flip for you = -$25 per flip for the stranger (zero-sum); over 100 fair flips the chance of ending behind is 1.76% (<2%); a single flip is 50/50.

math_check: You, per flip: 0.5*150 - 0.5*100 = +$25; the stranger pays the other side, so -$25 per flip on average. Felt loss = 1.955*100 = $195.50 -> 'about $195' (95% range $182.00-$210.20, all > $150). 100 flips: total = 150h - 100(100-h) = 250h - 10,000 < 0 iff h <= 39; P(h <= 39 | n=100, p=0.5) = 0.017600 = 1.76% -> 'almost never' spoken, '<2%' on screen. Line 5's lost first flip (-$100) is consistent: one flip is 50/50. Re-computed in python.
changes_from_previous: QA fix 1 (hook/stakes): lines 1-2 merged into one 13-word line 'What if a stranger offers: heads, win one fifty. Tails, lose a hundred?'. The offer starts at word 6 (~1.9 s) and the full +$150/-$100 is said by ~4.5 s. '+$150' is on screen from frame 0, the stranger holds the coin from frame 0, and '-$100' pops on 'Tails'.

QA fix 2 (twist logic) + fix 3 (open loop): 'he bet you'd run' is gone. Line 3 now plants 'Weird part? He's the one who should run.' and line 8 pays it off in the last ~5 s: 'Wait... the stranger gulps. Every flip costs him twenty five.' This follows from zero-sum EV (computed).

QA fix 4 (lecture in lines 5-8): two fact beats merged into one ('Your brain makes losing a hundred feel like about one ninety five'), with 'LOSS AVERSION ~2x' moved to an on-screen stamp. The rest is now action: Benny flips anyway, loses flip #1 (a flipcoin lands on his head, a TAILS -$100 stamp, camera shake, a tear), keeps flipping (a 3-coin flipcoin montage, '+$25 per flip' badge), and coin rain piles up as the 100 FLIPS counter runs. Facts are quick on-screen beats inside the action.

QA fix 5 (length): 89 -> 79 spoken words = ~30.4 s at 2.6 wps (~32 s with default pauses), safely inside 25-35 s. 9 lines, 10 scenes (the last line is split into the loop scene and the A/B list scene).
QA fix 6 (line 8 clarity): '100 flips? You almost never end up behind.' is said as a result; '<2% end behind' stays on screen.

QA fix 7 (ending): the deflating 'One flip's still fifty fifty' is no longer spoken. The ending re-says the offer to loop the hook ('Heads, one fifty. Tails, a hundred. A, flip. B, run. You?'), and '1 flip = 50/50' plus 'Not financial advice' are corner badges.
QA fix 8 (originality): the unique part is now Benny's arc. He runs, comes back, loses flip #1, keeps going, ends up on a coin pile, and the scary stranger is the one who gulps.

QA fix 9 (drawability): no brain shake (camera shake on the $195 stamp instead), no dropping prop (the head bonk is a flipcoin with x2/y2 at Benny's head), and 'sweating' is replaced with a spoken 'gulps' plus a 'GULP.' bubble and pose worry. Every visual uses documented items: flipcoin, coins, counter, stamp, bubble, badge, headline, list, camera shake/beats.
QA fix 10 (ph): 'Pustahan niya' is gone along with that line; line 3 ph uses 'Ang weird pa?' as suggested.
